software.message: Cedar Metrics sells reporting software to product managers. The goal is $15,000 monthly contribution within 90 days. Managers evaluate a demo, then choose a paid subscription. Current numbers are 1,000 qualified leads per month, 10 percent lead-to-paying conversion and $100 contribution per paying customer, giving $10,000 monthly contribution. These are the operating numbers for Cedar Metrics, a separate business from the professional profile. Keep the interview concise and focus on the next useful decision.
Reasons prospects decline are unknown. Keep that gap unknown and do not ask the reasons again. A clearer product-value message is a proposed intervention; the effect has not been measured.
Summarize the proposed model. Keep the observed baseline conversion at 10 percent. A possible 12 percent conversion is only a scenario, not an observed result. Do not run an experiment.

ice_cream.message: Cedar Cream sells tubs of ice cream in independent grocery stores. The goal is $10 million in annual sales by December 2027. Shoppers compare tubs, choose a tub to buy and later decide whether to buy again. The number of shoppers, conversion rate and repeat-purchase rate are unknown. This is a separate business from the professional profile. Ask only one material question at a time.
I do not know the shopper count or conversion rate. The unknown numbers must stay unknown. A clearer vanilla label is a proposed intervention, not a measured effect.

Correction: the target is $12 million in annual sales by December 2027, replacing $10 million. Keep the existing customer journey and unknown operating inputs. No extra questions or experiment execution.

services.message: Cedar Advisory sells consulting engagements to B2B software companies. The goal is six new signed engagements per quarter starting January 2027. A product leader accepts a discovery meeting, reviews a proposal, and decides whether to sign. Current meeting volume and proposal-to-signature conversion are unknown. This is a separate business from the professional profile. Focus on the decision and avoid immaterial details.

We do not know why proposals are rejected. Leave those reasons unknown. An existing customer may introduce another product leader; referrals are a hypothesis for improvement, not an established causal effect.

Prepare the proposed model using the stated customer journey and six-engagement quarterly goal. Keep meeting volume and conversion unknown. Suggest one material experiment without launching any paid study; no further questions.
